evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We distribute HIV self-test kits through 120 community pharmacies across 10 local government areas in Lagos. We want to test two changes: a subsidy that cuts the kit price from 2,000 to 500 naira, and a peer-referral voucher that lets a buyer give a free kit to a partner. Outcome: share of adult customers offered a kit who buy one, from the pharmacy log. The state program will decide whether to scale the subsidy, the voucher, or both to all 20 LGAs. Customers of the same pharmacy talk to each other, and vouchers travel to partners who may use another pharmacy in the same LGA. The state wants every pharmacy covered within 12 months; pharmacies can be delayed but not excluded. We can launch in all 120 at once. We can only offer the subsidy at the pharmacy, not assign who buys. We need to know whether the voucher adds anything beyond the subsidy. How should we randomize?
evals.expected_output: A trial design choice in the output template that randomizes pharmacies in a factorial design covering every pharmacy by month 12, with a named runner-up.
assertions: Rules out randomizing individual customers because of spillovers or a price set at the pharmacy.
Uses the pharmacy as the unit of randomization.
Chooses a factorial (or four-arm) design because the decision needs the voucher's value beyond the subsidy.
Treats every pharmacy by month 12 through a waitlist or stepped rollout.
Says how the assignment is drawn and recorded, and who agreed to the delay.
Names a runner-up and the condition that would make it the choice.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: We want to run an RCT of our savings SMS. What design should we use?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks its required questions about the test, spillovers, rollout, control, and components, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks whether the SMS could reach people not assigned to it, for instance through shared phones or groups.
Asks whether everyone must receive it eventually or some can go without.
Asks what decision the result will inform.
Does not produce the constraints table.
Does not recommend a design.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: The county agriculture office in Western Kenya wants to test SMS advice on fertilizer timing. They insist on randomizing at the sub-county level, there are 8 sub-counties, and the governor's office has said no sub-county can be left without the service. Farmers in the same group share phones and advice. What design?
evals.expected_output: The skill fills what it can, rejects an eight-sub-county design, proposes randomizing farmer groups within every sub-county, and tells the user to bring in an evaluation methodologist and the county authority.
assertions: Says eight sub-counties are too few to randomize as the unit.
Proposes randomizing farmer groups, or another unit below the sub-county, so every sub-county receives the service.
Gives shared phones and advice within a group as the reason the group, not the farmer, is the unit.
Tells the user to consult an evaluation methodologist.
Says to involve the county authority or an ethics board because the randomization is contested.
Says what to bring to the specialist.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: We have settled on randomizing 60 villages for the sanitation program, 30 per arm. How many households per village do we need to survey?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the design is chosen and the question is sample size, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the design and unit of randomization are already chosen.
Names estimate-sample-size.
Does not produce the constraints table.
